name: VerdeGo Design System
description: Design tokens and component patterns extracted from src/App.tsx (25-screen ride-share mockup for Monash University students/staff). Built with Tailwind CSS v4, React 19. Use this as the single source of truth when building new screens or components so they stay visually consistent with the existing app.

importSourceCaveats.note: This codebase was generated by Figma Make, which renders every screen inside a single interactive App.tsx as a clickable prototype. Several things in that file exist ONLY to let a human preview/demo the prototype in a browser - they are NOT part of the target mobile app's design or behavior. See demoOnlyElements below before treating anything in App.tsx as a literal spec. This is a MOBILE app (native or mobile-web) - every screen is meant to be its own full-screen route, not a section of a scrollable desktop page.
importSourceCaveats.generalRule: If an element in App.tsx exists to help you browse OR compare screens rather than to help an end user complete a ride-sharing task, it is demo chrome - exclude it from the real product.

product.name: VerdeGo
product.domain: Ride-sharing app exclusive to Monash University (Clayton campus) students & staff
keyFeatures: Green Score / CO2 tracking per ride (via 'Carbon Interface' data)
No surge pricing - fare = distance + live petrol price + flat platform fee
WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility explicitly called out in Settings

brand._usage: verde-500/600/700 are the primary brand greens used for CTAs, active states, headers. verde-50/100/200 used for tinted backgrounds/badges.

accent._usage: Pickup-point markers, star ratings, 'B' green-score tier, warning/notice banners.

neutral._usage: Standard Tailwind gray scale used for body text (gray-500/600), headings (gray-800/900), borders (gray-100/200), disabled/placeholder (gray-400).

error._usage: Report/cancel/decline/error flows only. Never mixed with brand green in the same control.

avatarPalettes._usage: Each user avatar is randomly/consistently assigned one bg+text pair from this list of Tailwind 100/700 pairs, used as flat initials avatars.

gradients._primaryCTAUsage: All primary action buttons (Continue, Confirm, Submit, Post, Accept, etc.)
gradients._headerHeroUsage: Top header bands on screens with a colored hero section (Home, Post flow, Requests, My Rides, Profile, Rating)
gradients._postFabUsage: Center 'Post' tab in bottom nav (raised circular FAB)
gradients._destructiveUsage: Only for the final 'Submit Report' button when a reason is selected

fontFamilies.heading: 'Poppins', sans-serif
fontFamilies.loadedFrom: Google Fonts, imported in src/index.css: Poppins (400,500,600,700,800) & Inter (400,500,600)

usageRules.Poppins: ALL headings (h1/h2), button labels, form labels, numeric/stat values (fares, scores, distances), navigation labels, badges, tab labels - anything that needs emphasis or is a UI 'label'.
usageRules.Inter: ALL body copy, descriptions, placeholders, helper/secondary text, input values, timestamps.

xs.usage: captions, meta info, badges, helper text

sm.usage: body text, form inputs, secondary buttons

weights._usage: font-semibold is the default for Poppins labels; font-bold for headings/CTAs; font-extrabold reserved for hero numbers (fare totals, app name).

spacing.screenPaddingX: px-5 (20px) is standard; px-6 (24px) used on auth/simple-form screens (Login, Verify, Report)
spacing.sectionGap: gap-3 (12px) to gap-5 (20px) between stacked cards/fields depending on density

borderRadius.full: rounded-full - pills, avatars, chips, dots, toggles
borderRadius.3xl: rounded-3xl (24px) - bottom-sheet modals, splash icon container, top of ride-detail sheet
borderRadius.2xl: rounded-2xl (16px) - DEFAULT for cards, buttons, inputs, banners, badgesheets. This is the dominant radius in the app.
borderRadius.xl: rounded-xl (12px) - secondary/inline elements: filter chips (segmented), stat tiles, smaller buttons, icon containers
borderRadius.lg: rounded-lg (8px) - focus-ring containers on icon-only buttons
borderRadius.custom: rounded-[52px] phone shell frame, rounded-[28px] grid thumbnail frame - decorative/mockup-chrome only, not reusable UI

tapTargets.rule: Minimum 44x44px for ALL interactive elements (buttons, toggles, icon buttons) - explicitly documented in-app as a WCAG 2.2 AA requirement.
tapTargets.smallToggleSwitchHeight: 28px height / 48px width (iOS-style switch - the one exception, still >44px touch area intended via parent)

elevation.shadow-sm: cards at rest (RideCard, list rows, settings groups)
elevation.shadow-md: primary CTA buttons, floating action elements
elevation.shadow-lg: splash CTA button, floating map pins/back buttons over imagery
elevation.shadow-2xl: phone device frame, bottom-sheet modals (highest elevation)
elevation.shadow (bare): map floating info cards, top nav overlay buttons

iconography.style: Custom hand-drawn inline SVG icons (NOT an icon library like lucide/heroicons). Consistent 1.5–2px stroke weight, rounded line caps/joins, viewBox typically 16x16, 20x20, or 24x24 depending on context.
iconography.colorPattern: Icons accept a `color` prop (hex string) and `size` prop (number, px) - never hardcoded Tailwind classes for icon fill/stroke.

set.name: CarIcon
set.usage: Bottom nav 'My Rides' tab, empty states, vehicle references

set.name: PlusIcon
set.usage: Bottom nav 'Post' FAB, add-photo affordance, seat stepper

set.name: LeafIcon
set.usage: Eco/green-score branding accent, CO2 callouts, app logo mark

set.name: MapPinIcon
set.usage: Destination markers (paired with amber dot for pickup points)

set.name: CheckIcon
set.usage: Success states, verified badges, accepted status

markerConvention.destination: Green MapPinIcon (#16a34a) - always represents Monash Clayton / drop-off (the fixed destination)

demoOnlyElements.note: Figma Make wraps every real screen in a single App.tsx so a human can click through the prototype in a browser. Everything below is part of THAT browsing harness, not the mobile app itself. Do not port these into the production build, and do not extract colors/spacing/components from them as if they were app UI.

items.where: App() root render, wraps every screen
items.detail: rounded-[52px] dark bezel, side buttons, dynamic island notch. Purely a 'this is what it'd look like on a phone' visual frame for the browser preview. The real app has no phone-frame chrome around its own screens - each screen simply IS the full device viewport.

items.element: Grid view / Single view toggle, Prev/Next arrows, and the quick-jump chip list
items.where: App() root render, bottom controls and top-right 'All Screens' button
items.detail: This is the 'drag down / scroll to see other screens' navigation the user is referring to - a flat prototype-browsing mechanism (array index +/-1, or a grid of all 25 thumbnails) so a reviewer can flip through every screen outside of the app's real logic. It does not represent real in-app navigation. The production app should use normal mobile navigation instead: a stack navigator (push/pop) for the linear flows (onboarding, post-a-ride wizard, ride detail) and the persistent BottomNav for switching between top-level sections (Feed/My Rides/Post/Requests/Profile) - never a manual 'screen index' switch or an exhaustive all-screens grid.
A cut-down, hardcoded re-render of each screen used only to draw the small preview cards in Grid view. Not a real screen and not a pattern to reuse.

Hardcoded '9:41' clock plus static signal/wifi/battery icons. This simulates the native iOS status bar purely so the mockup reads as 'a phone screen' in a browser. See components.StatusBar.productionNote.

The 7-day calendar strip (hardcoded dates 11-17, day 13 fixed as 'selected') and the Hour:Minute:Period boxes (hardcoded '08 : 15 : AM') are a static visual mock, not a working date/time picker - nothing is actually selectable/computed. A real implementation needs an actual interactive calendar (or native date picker) and a real time input, not hardcoded demo values. This is also likely what was meant by 'keyboard' scaffolding - visual placeholders standing in for real input controls.

Names (Priya Sharma, James Chen...), the fixed '9:41' clock, ride prices, CO2 figures, review text, and the 'Report reference #VG-2025-08-1042' are illustrative sample data for the mockup, not real content or a real ID format to preserve.

StatusBar.description: Fake iOS status bar (9:41, signal/wifi/battery icons) rendered at the top of every screen.
variants: light (light=true prop, text-white - used on colored hero headers)
StatusBar.productionNote: This is demo chrome standing in for the REAL native OS status bar (see demoOnlyElements). A real mobile build should not render its own fake clock/battery/signal - on native it's drawn by the OS, and on mobile-web it should just respect the device safe-area-inset-top. The only thing worth carrying into production is the `light` vs `dark` variant idea: on a colored hero header, the OS status bar's own light/dark content style (icons/text) should be set to light, matching the pattern used here.

BackButton.description: Chevron-left icon button, top-left of secondary/detail screens.

BottomNav.description: 5-tab fixed bottom navigation: Feed, My Rides, Post (raised gradient FAB), Requests, Profile.
BottomNav.activeIndicator: icon + label color change only (no underline/pill)
BottomNav.postTabException: Rendered as a 40x40 circular gradient button (postFabButton gradient), elevated with shadow-md, icon-only (no label).

Avatar.description: Circular initials avatar (first letter of first+last name, uppercased, max 2 chars).
Avatar.colorSource: avatarPalettes token set - bg + text pair

Stars.description: 1-5 star rating display, inline SVG, filled = amber-500 (#f59e0b), empty = gray-200 (#e5e7eb).
Stars.interactiveVariant: RatingScreen uses a larger (36px) hoverable/clickable version with the same fill logic

GreenScoreBadge.description: Small pill showing letter grade (A+/A/B/C) + CO2 text, colored per greenScoreBadge token.
GreenScoreBadge.usage: RideCard, MyRides card, UserProfile vehicle section

primary.disabledStyle: flat light background (e.g. #d1fae5) with muted text (e.g. #6ee7b7) instead of gradient - seen in RatingScreen 'Submit Review' before a star is picked

destructiveOutline.usage: Decline, Cancel Ride, Report an issue, report-reason radio rows

destructiveFilled.usage: Only the final confirm on ReportUserScreen once a reason is selected

iconButton.shape: circular or rounded-xl, white or white/90 bg, shadow, minWidth/minHeight 44px
iconButton.usage: map back button, favorite/heart button, close buttons

textField.labelStyle: text-sm font-semibold text-gray-700, Poppins, mb-2, block above field

segmentedControl.description: Row of equal-width pill/rounded buttons for mutually-exclusive filters or tabs (e.g. Eco/Cost/Time filter, passenger/driver/both role picker, upcoming/past tabs).
segmentedControl.activeStyle: solid brand-green background (or white pill on a colored hero header), white or verde-700 text, no border
segmentedControl.inactiveStyle: white/transparent background, gray-500/600 text, 1.5px gray-200 border (or white/70 text on colored headers)
segmentedControl.shape: rounded-full for filter chips, rounded-xl for role/tab pickers inside a rounded-2xl track

toggleSwitch.shape: w-12 h-6 track, w-5 h-5 white circular thumb, shadow on thumb

progressBar.description: Thin rounded bar showing step/completion progress (used in Post-a-Ride 4-step flow and Profile Setup).
progressBar.track: h-1.5 bg-gray-100 (or bg-white/30 on colored headers), rounded-full
progressBar.fill: gradient (verde-600→verde-500) or solid white on colored headers, rounded-full, width set by step %

card.default: bg-white, rounded-2xl, p-4, shadow-sm, border border-gray-100
card.usage: RideCard, request rows, my-rides rows, settings groups, review rows

calloutBanner.description: Colored info/warning/danger box with icon + bold micro-heading + supporting text, used constantly for contextual explanations.

variants.info-green: bg-green-50 (border border-green-200 optional), text-green-700 heading / text-green-600 body
variants.warning-amber: bg-amber-50 border border-amber-200, text-amber-700 heading / text-amber-600 body
variants.danger-red: bg-red-50 border border-red-100 (or border-red-100), text-red-600 heading / text-red-500 body

bottomSheetModal.description: Full-width sheet sliding from bottom, over a dimmed (bg-black/40) backdrop.
bottomSheetModal.dragHandle: w-10 h-1 bg-gray-300 rounded-full, centered, mb-5

radioSelectionList.description: Vertical list of selectable reason/option rows with a custom circular radio indicator.
radioSelectionList.selected: border-2 border-red-500 (context-dependent color), bg-red-50, text-red-500, filled radio dot

statTile.description: Small equal-width tiles in a row showing a stat/metric with label beneath.
statTile.shape: flex-1, rounded-xl, p-2 to p-3, text-center
statTile.usage: Ride detail quick facts, in-trip stats row

skeletonLoader.description: Loading placeholder using gray blocks with animate-pulse.
skeletonLoader.style: bg-gray-200 rounded, animate-pulse, sized to mimic real content (avatar circle + text lines)

mapBackground.description: Faux map pattern used behind route/location visuals (no real map integration).
mapBackground.style: background-color #e8f5e9 with a repeating 28x28px light-green grid line pattern
mapBackground.routeLines: SVG path, stroke #22c55e, strokeWidth 3-5, sometimes dashed (strokeDasharray '6,3') for planned routes vs solid for live in-trip routes

settingsListRow.description: Full-width tappable row: leading emoji/icon, label, trailing chevron.
settingsListRow.shape: px-4 py-3.5, minHeight 52px, border-b border-gray-100 between rows (last:border-0), grouped under a bg-white rounded-2xl container with an uppercase gray-400 xs section label

tagChip.description: Small pill for quick-select tags (e.g. rating review tags).
tagChip.style: rounded-full, border-2 border-green-200, bg-green-50, text-green-700, text-xs font-medium, px-3 py-1.5, minHeight 36px

interactionStates.focusVisible: Every interactive element has an explicit focus:outline-none focus:ring-{2|4} focus:ring-{color}-{300|400|500} - never relies on browser default outline. Ring color matches the element's semantic color (green for normal, red for destructive).
interactionStates.activeSelected: Selected state = solid brand gradient/color fill + white text (buttons/segments) OR colored border + tinted bg + colored text (cards/radio rows) - never uses opacity alone to indicate selection.
interactionStates.disabled: Muted flat pastel background + muted text color (e.g. bg-red-300/#fca5a5, bg-green pastel #d1fae5) rather than reduced opacity.

rules: Icons always paired with text labels (never icon-only without an accessible label in primary nav/actions)
Visible focus states on all interactive elements
Text size toggle offered (Normal/Large) as a user preference
High Contrast Mode toggle present in settings (scaffolded, not yet implemented)

screenInventory.note: 25 screens grouped by flow, each mapped to a requirement tag (R1-R7) in the source mockup. Useful for another agent to know what screens exist and what pattern group they belong to. The grouping below (onboarding, home, postRide, etc.) reflects real navigable app sections - it is independent of the flat prev/next/grid demo harness described in demoOnlyElements, which should not be reimplemented.

guidanceForNewScreens: Always split Poppins (labels/numbers/headings/buttons) vs Inter (body/descriptions/placeholders) per the usageRules above - don't mix.
Default card/button/input radius is rounded-2xl (16px) unless it's a small chip/tile (rounded-xl) or a pill (rounded-full).
Primary action = gradients.primaryCTA, full-width, 56px min height, bottom of screen (sticky footer pattern with border-t border-gray-100).
Any screen with a colored top section should use gradients.headerHero and pair it with StatusBar light + white/green-100/green-200 text.
Amber = pickup/departure and warnings. Green = destination, success, eco/positive metrics, primary actions. Red = destructive/safety only.
Every new interactive element needs a focus ring and a ≥44px tap target - this is a hard rule in this app, not optional polish.
Reuse existing components (Avatar, Stars, GreenScoreBadge, calloutBanner, statTile) rather than inventing new patterns for the same job.

Ignore/exclude everything listed in demoOnlyElements - the phone bezel, the grid/prev-next/quick-jump screen browser, the fake status-bar clock, and the static (non-functional) calendar/time picker are all Figma Make preview scaffolding, not part of the mobile app's real design or navigation model.

This is a mobile app: build one full-screen route per screen (native screen or mobile-web view at the device viewport), navigated via a stack navigator for linear flows and the BottomNav for top-level sections - never a scrollable desktop page or an index-based screen switcher.
